comment: Recognition layer 2: community signs. Coordinates are real-world lat/lon projected via route origin+scale at load time. radius is trigger distance in compressed-world meters. needs_owner_review: true means the coordinate or note was derived from map data, not lived knowledge — owner should verify before ship.

communities.name: Palisadoes
communities.note: The narrow sand spit stretching 10 km into Kingston Harbour

communities.name: Harbour View
communities.note: Eastern gateway to Kingston, where the Palisadoes meets the city

communities.name: Rockfort
communities.note: Named for the 17th-century English fortification on the hillside

communities.name: Vineyard Town
communities.note: Inner-city Kingston community along Mountain View Avenue

communities.name: Cross Roads
communities.note: Central Kingston junction where major roads converge

communities.name: Half Way Tree
communities.note: One of Kingston's busiest transport hubs, named for a historic cotton tree

communities.name: Three Miles
communities.note: Named for its distance from the town centre along Spanish Town Road

communities.name: Spanish Town
communities.note: Jamaica's first capital city, founded as Villa de la Vega in 1534

communities.name: Sligoville
communities.note: First free village established in Jamaica after emancipation, 1835

communities.name: Bog Walk
communities.note: Gateway to the Rio Cobre gorge and Flat Bridge

communities.name: Linstead
communities.note: Market town immortalised in the folk song 'Linstead Market'

communities.name: Ewarton
communities.note: Agricultural market town in the Rio Cobre valley

communities.name: Moneague
communities.note: St Ann crossroads at the foot of Mount Diablo

communities.name: Faith's Pen
communities.note: Jamaica's most famous roadside cookshop strip — jerk, roast yam and festival

communities.name: Fern Gully
communities.note: 3 km natural tunnel of tree fern and bamboo descending to Ocho Rios

communities.name: Ocho Rios
communities.note: Jamaica's north-coast cruise hub — journey's end
